title: Mount Misery via Rifle Range Road
lede: A quick up-and-back climb on fire trail from the edge of town to Mount Misery, short enough to walk or run before or after work.
description: An 8.8 km return climb on fire trail from Rifle Range Road at Glen Ayr, on the western edge of Mudgee, to the communication tower on Mount Misery. Short enough to walk or run before or after work.
hero_alt: The lights of Mudgee at dawn under a low bank of fog, with a range of hills silhouetted against an orange and pink sky

card.image_alt: A group of runners and their dogs heading down a dirt fire trail past a communication tower, with Mudgee spread out below at sunrise
card.blurb: A quick climb on fire trail from the edge of town to Mount Misery and back. Walk it or run it, before or after work.

facts.label: Region
facts.value: Western edge of Mudgee, Glen Ayr

intro: Mount Misery is the high ground right on Mudgee's western doorstep, and this is the quickest way up it. It's fire trail all the way from the edge of town, up and back the same way, so you can walk it or run it. It's short enough to fit in before or after work.

getting_there.intro: The walk starts on Rifle Range Road at Glen Ayr, on the western edge of Mudgee, just west of Faucett Drive.

options.heading: Rifle Range Road, Glen Ayr
options.text: Head out along Rifle Range Road. On the south side there are two gates: go past the first and park outside the second, which has a "Shut the Gate, Mate" sign. The second gate is the access road to the towers, not the road to the rifle range.

getting_there.note: The way up crosses private property, so stay on the fire trail and leave the gate as you found it.

walk_intro: The route follows the fire trail south from Rifle Range Road, climbs past the Translator and the communication towers, then follows the Mount Misery Trail west to the communication tower on Mount Misery. It's about 4.4 km each way on fire trail, with a few steep sections, and you come back the same way. For a longer day, the [Misery Traverse](/misery-traverse/) carries on from the top along the ridge to Hill End Road.

stops.heading: Rifle Range Road
stops.text: Go through the second gate, the one with the "Shut the Gate, Mate" sign, and head south on the access road to the towers, away from town and towards the hills. This first part crosses private property, so stay on the track.

stops.heading: The Translator
stops.text: The fire trail climbs steadily to the Translator and the communication towers on the first spur, then swings south along the ridge towards the radio mast. As you gain height, the views open up across the valley.
stops.image_alt: A walker in a red shirt looking through the eucalypts to a valley of farmland and hills lit orange by the low sun
stops.caption: Looking across the valley on the climb up Mount Misery

stops.heading: Mount Misery Trail
stops.text: At the radio mast, turn west onto the Mount Misery Trail. It follows the edge of Avisford Nature Reserve along the ridge to Mount Misery.

stops.heading: Mount Misery
stops.text: The trail ends at the communication tower on Mount Misery. From the top there are great views of Mudgee spread out below, with farmland running away to the ranges on the horizon.
stops.image_alt: Four walkers standing in tall grass on Mount Misery, looking out over the town of Mudgee and the farmland beyond
stops.caption: Mudgee from Mount Misery

stops.heading: Back to Rifle Range Road
stops.text:
Head back down the same fire trail to Rifle Range Road. It's downhill most of the way, so it makes a good run.

If you'd rather keep going, the [Misery Traverse](/misery-traverse/) follows the ridge north from Mount Misery to Hill End Road.
stops.image_alt: A group of runners and their dogs heading down a dirt fire trail past a communication tower, with Mudgee spread out below at sunrise
stops.caption: Running back down towards Mudgee

map.alt: Topographic map showing the route from Rifle Range Road at Glen Ayr, past the Translator and the radio mast, then west along the Mount Misery Trail to the communication tower on Mount Misery
map.caption: Approximate route in orange. Base map: Mudgee 8832-4N topographic map.

tips.heading: Navigation
tips.text: It's fire trail all the way, so navigation is straightforward. Carry a map or the GPX on your phone.

tips.heading: Private land
tips.text: The route crosses private property on the way up, so stay on the fire trail. Shut the gate behind you.

tips.heading: Water
tips.text: There's no water on the walk. Carry what you'll need, especially if you're running on a hot afternoon.

tips.heading: Respect the Country
tips.text: This is Wiradjuri Country. Look, but don't touch. Leave no trace.

tips.heading: Tell someone
tips.text: Leave your plans with someone. There's good phone coverage along the way.
